question: A money site charted the Bank of England's rate cuts from 2024 to 2025. Rates look to be in free fall. Where's the trick?
answer: In the axis, drawn from 3.9% to 5.3%, so 1.25 points look like a cliff. From zero, rates are still 40 times their 2020–21 floor of 0.1%. That matters to anyone whose cheap fixed deal ends: a £200,000 25-year mortgage costs about £800 a month at 1.5%, about £1,110 at 4.5%.
move: Before cheering a fall, ask where it stands against the long run.
ask: When I hear rates are falling, do I check what my own next deal will cost?

scene.headline: Interest rates tumble
scene.label: Bank Rate at the quarter's end
scene.found: Yes: the axis spans less than one and a half points.
scene.miss: That part is fair. Look at how much the axis covers.

misses.marks: The rates are right. It's the ruler that makes them plunge.
misses.headline: Rates did fall. The drawing decides how far it looks.

scene.name: The zoomed axis
scene.lesson: A tight axis turns a step into a cliff. Read the range before the slope.

source: Bank of England, Bank Rate history
reference: Bank of England, Official Bank Rate history (0.1% March 2020 to December 2021; 5.25% August 2023; cuts August 2024 to August 2025); mortgage payments by the standard annuity formula
